title: Cranmer's two hinges of the day
hookLine: the prayer book's two daily offices, morning prayer and evening prayer
carry: prayer hangs on morning and evening

lines: EVENING, AND MORNING, AND AT NOON.
ONE LAMB AT MORNING, ONE AT EVENING.
cards: "Evening, and morning, and at noon, will I pray, and cry aloud: and he shall hear my voice." That's Psalm fifty-five, someone in real trouble, hanging their prayers on the clock.
In Exodus, too, one lamb is offered in the morning and another at evening, day by day. The day has two hinges: getting up and lying down.
The Church of England's Book of Common Prayer built on them, with The Order for Morning Prayer and The Order for Evening Prayer, daily throughout the year.
Today the Anglican way of prayer begins, with a door at each end of the day.

teach.b: Day one hundred seven gave the daily office a first look; here's its shape in the old prayer book. Morning Prayer opens with lines of scripture and a confession said together, and soon comes a short exchange.
The minister says, "O Lord, open thou our lips." The people answer, "And our mouth shall shew forth thy praise."

Then psalms, an Old Testament reading, a song, a New Testament reading, another song, the creed, the Lord's Prayer, and short prayers called collects. Evening Prayer has the same bones, with its own songs and collects.
The book lays out the psalms so the whole Psalter is read through each month. Now the last collect on each side of the day.

teach.h: BROUGHT TO THE BEGINNING OF THIS DAY.
teach.b: In the morning: "O Lord, our heavenly Father, Almighty and everlasting God, who hast safely brought us to the beginning of this day."
At night: "Lighten our darkness, we beseech thee, O Lord; and by thy great mercy defend us from all perils and dangers of this night." One says thank you for getting to the morning.
The other, at the door of the dark, asks for keeping.

Tradition says Thomas Cranmer, the archbishop who shaped the English prayer book, folded the monastery's many hours of prayer into these two, so a farmer or a shopkeeper could keep them as well as a monk.

Psalm ninety-two already had the idea: "To shew forth thy lovingkindness in the morning, and thy faithfulness every night." Some Anglicans pray the full offices in church, some at a kitchen table, some only the collects.
The length can change. The two hinges stay.

how: In the Anglican tradition, Morning and Evening Prayer from the Book of Common Prayer or a newer prayer book are said or sung daily in some cathedrals and parishes, and some clergy and lay people pray them on their own at home.

games.q: the minister says, "O Lord, open thou our lips." you're in the congregation. what comes next?
o: "and our mouth shall shew forth thy praise."
games.why: the people answer, "And our mouth shall shew forth thy praise": the day opens with a line from Psalm 51, said back and forth.

practice: In the morning, take the old opening line, O Lord, open thou our lips; in the evening, the night one, lighten our darkness.
If you pray, let the line be your prayer for a while; if you don't, simply hold it and notice the hinge of the day turning.
